TITLE: Using server-side-apply for an Ingress failed when updating IngressBackend from port number to port name
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

I created an Ingress resource with a port number manually, and then tried to use an Operator with server-side apply to update the resource from a port number to a port name. This failed with the error message "cannot set both port name & port number".

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the port number to be cleared as the operator would take over the ownership of the ServiceBackendPort. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

To simulate the behavior in the operator in a most simple example I use `kubectl`:

ingress-v1.yaml:

```
kind: Ingress
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: myingress
spec:
  defaultBackend:
    service:
      name: myservice
      port:
        number: 8443
```

ingress-v2.yaml:

```
kind: Ingress
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: myingress
spec:
  defaultBackend:
    service:
      name: myservice
      port:
        name: http
```

```
kubectl apply -f  ingress-v1.yaml --server-side --field-manager=app-1 --validate=false
kubectl apply -f  ingress-v2.yaml --server-side --field-manager=app-2 --validate=false  --force-con
ROOT CAUSE: The bug happened because the server-side apply merge strategy for the ServiceBackendPort struct was not set to 'atomic'. This caused conflicting updates when one updater set the port number and another tried to set the port name, leading to the error when both fields appeared to be set simultaneously. The lack of atomic merge meant that partial updates conflicted rather than one owner taking exclusive control of the entire port specification.
FIX: Changed how the API server handles updates to `.spec.defaultBackend` of Ingress objects.
Server-side apply now considers `.spec.defaultBackend` to be an atomic struct.  This means that any field-owner who sets values in that struct (they are mutually exclusive) owns the whole struct. For almost all users this change has no impact; for controllers that want to change the default backend port from number to name (or vice-versa), this makes it easier.
FILES: api/openapi-spec/swagger.json, api/openapi-spec/v3/apis__networking.k8s.io__v1_openapi.json, pkg/generated/openapi/zz_generated.openapi.go, staging/src/k8s.io/api/networking/v1/generated.proto, staging/src/k8s.io/api/networking/v1/types.go, staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/applyconfigurations/internal/internal.go

TITLE: Mismatched URLs for service-account-issuer-discovery and Open API Spec's swagger.json
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

When I use the official Kubernetes Java Client (version 18.0.0) from within a pod using `Config.defaultClient()` to build an `ApiClient` and then access `getServiceAccountIssuerOpenIDConfiguration` in the `WellKnownApi` I get the following error:

```json
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:test:user\" cannot get path \"/.well-known/openid-configuration/\"",
  "reason": "Forbidden",
  "details": {},
  "code": 403
}
```

The same happens with the `OpenidApi#getServiceAccountIssuerOpenIDKeyset`.

However, the problem does not happen when I call the `/.well-known/openid-configuration` endpoint using the pod's service account and curl.

The problem is that the generated Open API spec indicates that the client should call `/.well-known/openid-configuration/` instead of `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (and similarly `/openid/v1/jwks/` instead of `/openid/v1/jwks`). While the API Server seems to resolve these endpoints just fine, the `ClusterRole` defined in the code does not have the trailing slashes and therefore rejects the requests with a 
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is that the ClusterRole for service-account-issuer-discovery defines permissions for nonResourceURLs without trailing slashes, but the OpenAPI spec (swagger.json) documents these URLs with trailing slashes. This mismatch causes RBAC authorization to fail for legally formed requests that append a trailing slash, since the policy does not allow those exact paths.
FIX: Add slash ended urls for service-account-issuer-discovery to match API in swagger
FILES: plugin/pkg/auth/authorizer/rbac/bootstrappolicy/policy.go, plugin/pkg/auth/authorizer/rbac/bootstrappolicy/testdata/cluster-roles.yaml

TITLE: Cannot create ingress with ingressClass annotation and IngressClassName both set
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

An ingress resource with both `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` set cannot be **created**. Ingress resources can be updated to include both the annotation and the `ingressClassName` without issue.

Kubernetes response:

> The Ingress "example-ingress" is invalid: annotations.kubernetes.io/ingress.class: Invalid value: "nginx": can not be set when the class field is also set


### What did you expect to happen?

The ingress should be deployed with both annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` set, as it is supported by updating an existing ingress.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Apply this resource:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: example-ingress
  annotations:
    ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: "nginx"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: test.foo.bar
    http:
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          backend:
            service:
              name: dummy-service
              port:
                number: 1234

```

### Anything else we ne
ROOT CAUSE: The ingress validation logic incorrectly disallowed creating new ingress resources that have both the "kubernetes.io/ingress.class" annotation and the "spec.ingressClassName" field set, despite this being supported for updates. This strict validation effectively prevented creation of such ingress objects, causing the bug.
FIX: Ingress with ingressClass annotation and IngressClassName both set can be created now.
FILES: pkg/apis/networking/validation/validation.go, pkg/apis/networking/validation/validation_test.go, pkg/registry/networking/ingress/strategy.go

TITLE: [KCCM]: service update while node sync is processing might impact ingress  
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

The Kubernetes cloud controller manager uses resource watchers to sync load balancers, a Node/Service watcher. The Node watcher is slower by nature since any Node event will sync all service load balancers on the cluster. The service watcher is quicker since it only syncs the service load balancer which the event relates to. 

How slow a Node sync is will vary on the cluster, i.e: amount of Services of `type: LoadBalancer` and Nodes, but on big clusters with a lot of churn: the time to process one Node sync can be sufficiently slow to have the cache of Nodes go stale w.r.t the actual cluster state. The cache of Nodes is here the resource informer cache. When syncing Nodes the Node control loop will list all Nodes in its cache and then iterate over all Services and sync their load balancers in parallel, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L799-L818

If any Service experiences an update needing a load balancer sync, the Service controller will also list the Nodes in the informer cache, but retrieve a more up-to-date copy, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is that the node sets keyed per service were not synchronized between the service and node control loops, causing transient addition and removal of nodes in load balancer backend sets during concurrent node and service syncs. Because lastSyncedNodes was shared globally rather than per service, parallel syncs conflicted, leading to stale node removals after additions.
FIX: KCCM: fix transient node addition + removal caused by #121090 while syncing load balancers on large clusters with a lot of churn
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go, staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller_test.go, staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/fake/fake.go

TITLE: Named ports specified in sidecar container pod spec are not available to services
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

When migrating a sidecar container to a native sidecar container (initContainer with restartPolicy=Always), traffic going via the Kubernetes Service did not reach the application container/sidecar container.

### What did you expect to happen?

The traffic should have reached the sidecar container like before the migration.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a Pod with a native sidecar container (initContainer) with a named port, as well as a Kubernetes Service using that named port as its targetPort. This port is not listed in the Endpoint.

Apply the following:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sidecar-ports
  labels:
    app: sidecar-ports
spec:
  containers:
  - image: bloomberg/goldpinger:3.10.1
    name: goldpinger
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8000
      name: http
      protocol: TCP
  initContainers:
  # note: no envoy configuration is provided, the steps to reproduce involve reading other Kubernetes manifests (Endpoints)
  - image: envoyproxy/envoy:v1.73.7
    name: tls-terminator
    ports:
    - containerPort: 9443
      name: https
      protocol: TCP
--
ROOT CAUSE: The Kubernetes endpoint controller did not consider named ports declared in initContainers with restartPolicy=Always as available ports for Services endpoints. This omission caused Services targeting those named ports to not have corresponding ports listed in their Endpoints resource, preventing traffic from reaching the sidecar container through the Service.
FIX: The name port of the sidecar will also be allowed to be used
FILES: pkg/api/v1/pod/util.go, pkg/api/v1/pod/util_test.go

diagnosis.root_cause: The bug occurs because the RelaxedServiceNameValidation feature gate check logic depends on the 'allowRelaxedServiceNameValidation' function which only permits relaxed validation if the feature gate is enabled or if the existing ingress's service names meet relaxed validation criteria. Although the user claims the 'spec.defaultBackend' service name is not checked, the code actually checks it along with the service names in 'spec.rules'. Therefore, the observed inconsistent behavior arises not from omission of defaultBackend service name validation, but from the interaction of this check with feature gate state and service name validation logic.

claims.text: The 'allowRelaxedServiceNameValidation' function performs relaxed validation for both 'spec.defaultBackend.service.name' and all service names in 'spec.rules' HTTP paths.
The function short-circuits and returns true if the RelaxedServiceNameValidation feature gate is enabled, allowing all such validation.

If the feature gate is disabled, the function checks if any existing service name in the ingress meets relaxed validation criteria and allows validation only in that case; otherwise, it returns false.

The user-reported issue arises since an ingress created with relaxed validation enabled (thus permitting service names starting with digits) becomes invalid for update when the feature gate is disabled, causing validation to fail for those names.

TITLE: Scheduler will run into race conditions on large scale clusters
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

The scheduler has a [30s timeout](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0fefe4e605ba05793e919598c09390769c127b3c/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L231) for the bind operation to succeed; if we don't get a response within 30s, the in-memory assignment of pod to node in the [scheduler cache expires](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0fefe4e605ba05793e919598c09390769c127b3c/pkg/scheduler/internal/cache/cache.go#L720).

A race condition will happen in the follow case:

1. pod1 is assigned to a node, scheduler cache is updated with the assignment, bind operation issued to apiserver.

1. if the apiserver is under huge pressure, bind takes more than 30s, scheduler expires the cached pod-to-node assignment.

1. bind eventually succeeds, but because the apiserver is under huge pressure, the pod update with the node name takes a long time to propagate to the scheduler.

TITLE: CRD validation allows invalid CABundles that will fail setting up handlers
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

A CRDs with an invalid conversion webhook CABundle failed to serve requests not requiring conversion.

### What did you expect to happen?

Since creating cr-1.yaml doesn't require conversion, I would have expected either:

1. An error response when attempting to create/update the CRD with an invalid CABundle
2. Only an error when conversion is required to server a request

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


Create a mult-version CRD with a conversion webhook configured with an invalid CABundle:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: replicant.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                myfield:
                  type: integer
    - name: v2
      served: true
      storage: false
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              ty
ROOT CAUSE: The bug happened because the CRD validation logic allowed invalid or non-PEM-encoded CABundles to be accepted when creating or updating CustomResourceDefinitions. This caused failures later when setting up conversion webhook handlers, which expect a valid CA certificate bundle for secure communication. Without proper validation at CRD creation time, invalid CABundles lead to internal errors and prevented serving requests properly.
FIX: CustomResourceDefinition objects created with non-empty `caBundle` fields which are invalid or do not contain any certificates will not appear in discovery or serve endpoints until a valid `caBundle` is provided. Updates to CustomResourceDefinition are no longer allowed to transition a valid `caBundle` field to an invalid `caBundle` field, because this breaks serving of the existing CustomResourceDefinition.
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/validation/validation.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/validation/validation_test.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/controller/establish/establishing_controller.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/test/integration/cabundle_test.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/validation.go, staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/validation_test.go

TITLE: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy using CRDs as paramKind always fails after restarting kube-apiserver
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

I'm using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy(VAP) with setting my own CRD to paramKind in my on-premise cluster. It works fine, but once I restarted one of the kube-apiserver instances it changed to reject both valid and invalid requests with the error message like:

```
error: failed to create rolebinding: rolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "view" is forbidden: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'test-vap' denied request: failed to configure policy: failed to find resource referenced by paramKind: 'example.com/v1alpha1, Kind=Foo'
```

### What did you expect to happen?

VAP using CRDs as paramKind should continue to work fine even when one of kube-apiserver instances is restarted.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You can reproduce it locally using kind cluster by following procedure.

<details>

```
$ cat kind.yaml         
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
  kubeadmConfigPatches:
  - |
    kind: ClusterConfiguration
    apiServer:
      extraArgs:
        feature-gates: "ValidatingAdmissionPolicy=true"
        runtime-config: "admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
ROOT CAUSE: The bug occurred because the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy reconciliation logic would skip reprocessing a policy if it was unchanged, even if the previous attempt to sync the policy's paramKind informer (based on a CRD) had failed. This caused the system not to retry the informer creation after a kube-apiserver restart, resulting in the failure to find the resource referenced by paramKind.
FIX: Fixed a bug in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that caused policies which were using CRD parameters to fail to synchronize
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/validatingadmissionpolicy/controller_reconcile.go, test/integration/apiserver/cel/validatingadmissionpolicy_test.go

TITLE: Conntrack cleaning happens before network programming endpoints
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

Currently kube-proxy efficiently cleans all stale conntrack entries preventing traffic black holing for deleted endpoints, but there can be some corner cases when conntrack cleaning happens before programming the network leaving a small window in which if any packet arrives will back-hole the traffic.

The corner case:
Taking a simple case of load-balancer service backed by a deployment with single replica, on deleting the pod(gracefully), I observed two **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocations:
1.  First one with EndpointConditions.Ready as false
2. EndpointSlice was cleared for the pod 

The conntrack flow for this case:
1. After processing the first **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocation **EndpointsMap** will still have entries for the pod as endpoint still exists, though not in ready state so proxier won't program deletion of endpoint from the data path. But the endpoint IP will be picked for conntrack cleaning as new endpoint != old endpoint because of the not ready condition.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95e915c4288eda15da1724989f3f7dec9f3512d6/pkg/proxy/endpoints.go#L423-L436
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95e915c4288e
ROOT CAUSE: The bug occurred because the conntrack cleaning logic considers endpoint readiness changes as an indication to clean stale connections before the network datapath has been updated to reflect those changes. This causes a timing window where conntrack entries are cleaned ahead of actual network programming, potentially blackholing traffic.
FIX: Fix stale conntrack flow detection logic
FILES: pkg/proxy/endpoints.go, pkg/proxy/endpoints_test.go, pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go, pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier_test.go, pkg/proxy/types.go

TITLE: endpointslicemirroring controller not create endpointslice when the endpoints are recreate
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

* create a service without selector, and manual create endpoints for this service
* endpointslicemirroring controller will create an endpointslice for this service.
* after endpoint slice created, and kube-controller-manager restart.
* during the kube-controller-manager restart, the endpoint was deleted and recreated

### What did you expect to happen?

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* create a service without selector, and manual create endpoints for this service
* endpointslicemirroring controller will create an endpointslice for this service.
* after endpoint slice created, and kube-controller-manager restart.
* during the kube-controller-manager restart, the endpoint was deleted and recreated

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# paste output here
v 1.30.0
```

</details>

### Cloud provider

<det
ROOT CAUSE: The bug happened because after the kube-controller-manager restart, the internal tracker (endpointSliceTracker) that tracks EndpointSlices is empty, causing the controller to incorrectly reconcile the state. This leads to a failure to recreate EndpointSlices when the Endpoints resource is deleted and recreated during the restart. The controller did not properly synchronize its internal state from the existing EndpointSlice resources upon restart, resulting in missing EndpointSlice creation triggers.
FIX: Fix: during the kube-controller-manager restart, when the corresponding Endpoints resource was manually deleted and recreated, causing the endpointslice to fail to be created normally.

TITLE: endpoints not configured with MinimizeIPTablesRestore
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

To test out the MinimizeIPTablesRestore feature enabled in 1.27 by default we enabled the setting in 1.26 and discovered that it appears to not configure endpoints properly everytime.
While the version in 1.26 is still alpha I have not found any significant changes, bug reports or backports in the changelog regarding this.

It seems sometimes kube-proxy does not see that the endpoints of a service need to be updated despite the api endpointslice having changed. This typically is not that visible with externalTrafficPolicy Cluster services as some other endpoint still is configured, but in the case of low replica services or externalTrafficPolicy Local services this can lead to service disruption due to the only endpoint on the local node not getting configured while other components see the update correctly and direct traffic there.


For example this two pod deployment both pods ready since hours:

```
$ kubectl -n ns get pods pod1 pod2-o yaml | grep -B 2 Ready
      lastTransitionTime: "2023-10-19T10:21:19Z"
      status: "True"
      type: Ready
--
      lastTransitionTime: "2023-10-19T10:21:19Z"
      status: "True"
      type: ContainersRe
ROOT CAUSE: The bug was caused by a race condition in kube-proxy's iptables mode partial sync logic, where `syncProxyRules` made separate calls to check for pending updates and then apply them. Since the change trackers use their own mutexes independent from the proxier's, a new event could be processed between these calls, leading to inconsistent state and some endpoint updates being missed.
FIX: Fixes a race condition in the iptables mode of kube-proxy in 1.27 and later
that could result in some updates getting lost (e.g., when a service gets a
new endpoint, the rules for the new endpoint might not be added until
much later).
FILES: pkg/proxy/endpoints.go, pkg/proxy/endpoints_test.go, pkg/proxy/endpointslicecache.go, pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go, pkg/proxy/service.go, pkg/proxy/service_test.go

TITLE: kube-proxy nftables mode failed to delete rules due to "Device or resource busy" consistently in some cases
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

While validating nftable mode using conformance test, the following error logs were produced consistently:
```
E0104 17:21:56.957351       1 proxier.go:941] "Unable to delete stale chains; will retry later" err=<
        /dev/stdin:1:28-90: Error: Could not process rule: Device or resource busy
        delete chain ip kube-proxy service-QZNVUP4F-endpointslice-3291/example-named-port/tcp/http
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        /dev/stdin:3:28-109: Error: Could not process rule: Device or resource busy
        delete chain ip kube-proxy endpoint-A6Z5NSSV-endpointslice-3291/example-named-port/tcp/http__10.244.2.28/3001
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

I0104 18:43:05.900199       1 proxier.go:935] "Deleting stale nftables chains" numChains=1
E0104 18:43:05.945300       1 proxier.go:941] "Unable to delete stale chains; will retry later" err=<
        /dev/stdin:1:28-93: Error: Could not process rule: Device or resource busy
        delete chain ip kube-proxy endpoint-EVHUKXWZ-services-4440/externa
ROOT CAUSE: The bug occurred because a chain that was once identified as stale and added to the staleChains set could subsequently become active again. However, the proxier does not remove such chains from staleChains when they become active. Consequently, the proxier attempts to delete these chains even though they are currently active, causing errors indicating "Device or resource busy". The proxier's failure to update staleChains to reflect the chain's active status causes invalid deletion attempts.

TITLE: kube-proxy: initialization check race leads to stale UDP conntrack
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

AKS had a customer report repeated issues in their clusters where:
1. kube-proxy would redeploy (e.g. due to AKS deploying a new kube-proxy image with CVE fixes)
2. Envoy c-ares DNS client would send repeated DNS queries to the kube-dns service VIP from the same src IP address, creating a UDP conntrack entry to the svc VIP and keeping it alive. For example, with kube-dns svc VIP 192.168.0.10, conntrack showed:
```
# conntrack -L | grep 192.168.0.10 | grep UNREPLIED
udp      17 29 src=10.120.1.150 dst=192.168.0.10 sport=49660 dport=53 [UNREPLIED] src=192.168.0.10 dst=10.120.1.150 sport=53 dport=49660 mark=0 use=1
conntrack v1.4.5 (conntrack-tools): 2273 flow entries have been shown
```

3. DNS queries to the svc VIP were blackholed until the customer manually ran a command like: `conntrack -D -p udp --src 10.120.1.150 --sport 49660`

Issue occurred only in clusters with many services and endpoints (~10k services and ~6k endpoints). However, the customer has seen this issue repeatedly for months, about 1-5 times per week across their clusters.

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy code to delete stale UDP conntrack entries should have de
ROOT CAUSE: Kube-proxy was marking its initialization as complete before all service and endpointslice updates had been fully processed and delivered. This led to incomplete service state, causing transient removal of service rules and failure to clean up stale UDP conntrack entries.
FIX: Fix race condition in kube-proxy initialization that could blackhole UDP traffic to service VIP.
FILES: pkg/proxy/config/config.go

diagnosis.root_cause: The bug occurs because the winkernel proxier's RemoteEndpoint cleanup logic is conditional and skips proper cleanup under certain conditions, especially when multiple Services reference the same Deployment. This causes stale RemoteEndpoints to persist when Deployments or Pods are deleted, and the cleanup mechanism does not synchronize properly under high concurrency and large scale, resulting in missed deletions of RemoteEndpoints.

claims.text: The RemoteEndpoint cleanup in winkernel proxier is skipped conditionally when certain annotations or optimizations are enabled, leading to inconsistent cleanup of RemoteEndpoints on endpoint updates or deletions, as shown in pkg/proxy/winkernel/proxier.go.

The issue likely involves a logic defect in how RemoteEndpoint cleanup is coordinated among multiple Services referencing the same Deployment/Pods, leading to stale RemoteEndpoints persisting especially at scale and concurrency due to incomplete cleanup triggers.

TITLE: Kubelet panic when allocates device for pods.
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

It is suspected to be a concurrent bug of kubelet.

When we delete the last pod that requires GPU on the node and create two or more pods that require GPU at the same time, kubelet may panic on `allocateContainerResources` as following.

I think it's a concurrency issue.

1. Create a pod with GPU request, then kubelet will allocate resource for it. Kubelet try call device plugin to choose preferred device for it. **It will unlock the mutex!.** https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L984-L1006
2. Then we delete the last pod that requires GPU.
3. Create the second pod with GPU request, kubelet will allocate resource for it also. Kubelet will call `UpdateAllocatedDevices` to recalculate device (delete allocated device if pod deleted). It will update the **allocatedDevices** map of ManagerImpl, because of mutex is unlock by step 1. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L519-L543
4.  Kubelet continues with the first pod. If **allocatedDevices** has changed and GPU device is nil, kubelet will panic in the closure allocateRemainingFrom.

```
Jul 25 1
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is a concurrency race in kubelet's device manager when allocating GPU devices to pods. The mutex guarding the allocated devices map is unlocked while calling out to device plugins, allowing concurrent updates and leading to inconsistent or nil map values. This causes the allocation function to panic due to nil map assignments when multiple GPU-using pods are created or deleted concurrently.
FIX: Fix kubelet panic when allocate resource for pod.
FILES: pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go, pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager_test.go

A pod uses a PVC with volumeMode: Block. The block volume is backed by a block device on the node (which is created by some CSI storage providers).  If the node operating system is powered off , if the user delete the pod or the pod be eviceted by kcm, And then restarting the node, The pod would be stuck in terminating forever since Kubelet refuses to UnmapBlockVolume. kubelet  cannot delete the pod successfully.  

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should be able to finish terminating a pod  

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1.Install a CSI storage provider that supports volumeMode: Block.

2.Deloy a pod that has volumeClaimTemplates with volumeMode: Block. 

```

spec:

TITLE: Memory leak in kubelet volume_manager populator processedPods
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

If a pod is created and then deleted an entry in processedPods map remains forever (sometimes, it's racy).

The problem comes from the fact that `podWorker` calls volume_manager `WaitForUnmount()` asynchronously. If the last call happens after populator cleaned up resources, an entry is added to processedPods and will never be seen.

### What did you expect to happen?

An entry in processedPods map must be deleted if pod doesn't exist and pod runtime should removed according to `dswp.podStateProvider`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

To verify that the issue really exists I applaied a simple [patch](https://github.com/jsafrane/kubernetes/commit/40ffc8e62836244ea6cffde8b9dff2c402d058c5) printing resources in `processedPods` map. Here is a reproducer:

1. Start brand-new fresh k8s cluster with `hack/local-up-cluster.sh`
2. Check entries in `processedPods`:
```
I0321 15:03:42.131049    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod ac109c78-ce77-4426-9421-53fbcfe2175b: true
I0321 15:03:43.131815    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:262] JSAF: processed pods size: 1
```
3. Create a pod, chec
ROOT CAUSE: The volume_manager's podWorker calls WaitForUnmount asynchronously. If the final asynchronous call happens after the populator has cleaned up its resources, a pod UID is added to the processedPods map but the populator no longer tracks that pod. This pod entry then remains in processedPods indefinitely because the cleanup code only processes pods currently tracked by the volume_manager's internal cache.
FIX: Fix memory leak in kubelet volume_manager populator processedPods

diagnosis.root_cause: The fatal concurrent map write error occurs because the emptydir volume plugin's teardownDefault function calls fsquota.ClearQuota without appropriate synchronization. When pods with emptyDir volumes are created and deleted concurrently, multiple goroutines invoke ClearQuota that internally accesses and writes shared maps concurrently without locking, leading to concurrent map writes and program panic.

claims.text: The bug happens in emptydir's teardownDefault function which calls fsquota.ClearQuota without synchronization when the feature gate LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring is enabled.

The stack trace shows the concurrent map write occurs inside fsquota.ClearQuota called from empty_dir.go's teardownDefault function, triggered by concurrent pod create/delete operations with emptyDir volumes.

Past incident kb-119560 shows concurrency issues in kubelet volume management code can lead to panics and errors due to improper synchronization of shared maps accessed concurrently by multiple goroutines.

SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

diff --git a/test/e2e/dra/test-driver/deploy/example/pod-inline.yaml b/test/e2e/dra/test-driver/deploy/example/pod-inline.yaml

SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

```
E0126 00:39:45.253562       1 fieldmanager.go:210] "[SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields" err="failed to convert new object (default/test-inline-claim; /v1, Kind=Pod) to smd typed: .spec.containers[name=\"with-resource\"].resources.claims: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" VersionKind="/, Kind=" namespace="default" name="test-inline-claim"

```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected those lines not to appear in kube-apiserver logs, and structured-merge-diff to support map types, like the comment says at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/sigs.k8s.io/structured-merge-diff/v4/typed/helpers.go#L233

diagnosis.root_cause: The performance regression is caused by the increased overhead in handling the AllocationModeAll filtering behavior for resource pools during the slice conversion process in the dynamic resource allocation (DRA) code. Specifically, for each resource pool, the code converts all slices and filters them by node name, resulting in repeated and potentially expensive iterations over all resource slices across pools, which grows significantly with the number of pools and slices, especially when there are many multi-node resource pools. This mechanism leads to a performance regression in scheduling benchmarks that use SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate with multi-node resource pools.

claims.text: The code at staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/stable/pools_stable.go implements AllocationModeAll handling by calling convertSlices which filters slices by nodeName, iterating over all slices in each pool regardless of relevance.

The performance regression in SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate benchmarks coincides with the introduction of multi-node resource pools handling in commit 2e534d6da10, which uses AllocationModeAll and this convertSlices filtering approach, causing more work per scheduling loop.

TITLE: removeMissingExtendedResources() did not remove unknown extension resources from InitContainer
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

The function removeMissingExtendedResources() located at pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/predicate.go:217, is designed to remove any extended resources from a container’s requests that are not found in nodeInfo.Allocatable before the pod is admitted. This is necessary to support cluster-level resources, which are extended resources that are unknown to nodes.
However, this function only removes missingExtendedResources from the container’s requests, and does not process the requests of initContainers. This could lead to issues, as initContainers might request resources that do not exist on the node, which could result in the pod failing to be admitted or other unforeseen issues. As such, it may be necessary to refine the removeMissingExtendedResources() function to also handle initContainer’s requests.

### What did you expect to happen?

Refine the removeMissingExtendedResources() function to also handle initContainer’s requests.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a pod that requests cluster-level extended resources in both the container and InitContainer.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes versi
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause of the bug was that the removeMissingExtendedResources() function was incomplete in its processing scope; it only sanitized the extended resource requests of regular containers but neglected to perform the same cleanup for initContainers. Since initContainers can also request extended resources unknown to the node, this omission led to potential resource mismatches and pod admission failures.
FIX: Remove missing extended resources from init containers

TITLE: ResourceClaimParametersRef.APIGroup allows APIversion values
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

Following YAML file is accepted without error. Notice the `spec.parametersRef.apiGroup` field, it is an `APIVersion` instead of `APIGroup`, containing `/` character. This can lead to an issue when resource driver generates structured parameters' in-tree `ResourceClaimParameters` object with `generatedFrom.apiGroup` being just `APIGroup` without version. The DRA scheduler plugin will try to match the parameters object based on the reference here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/be4afb9ef90b19ccb6f7e595cbdb247e088b2347/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/dynamicresources/dynamicresources.go#L1066

In latest master the code appears to use an indexer, and the issue might be hidden, if applicable at all. I did not check the reproducibility in master yet. However, main question is whether the `APIGroup` should allow `APIVersion` value with `/` character in general.

```YAML
apiVersion: gpu.resource.intel.com/v1alpha2
kind: GpuClaimParameters
metadata:
  name: delayed-claim-external-gpu
spec:
  count: 1
  type: "gpu"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: delayed-claim-external-gpu
spec:
  resourceCl
ROOT CAUSE: The ResourceClaimParametersReference API allows an invalid value in the apiGroup field where an API version string (which contains a '/') is accepted instead of a valid API group name. This incorrect acceptance is due to missing validation constraints on the apiGroup field, which allows API version values containing characters like '/'. This leads to issues when resource driver generated parameters and the scheduler plugin try to match references by apiGroup but only expect a proper group without version suffixes.
FIX: DRA: enhance validation for the ResourceClaimParametersReference and ResourceClassParametersReference with the following rules:

1. `apiGroup`: If set, it must be a valid DNS subdomain (e.g. 'example.com').
2. `kind` and `name`: It must be valid path segment name. It may not be '.' or '..' and it may not contain '/' and '%' characters.

diagnosis.root_cause: The bug occurs due to the removal of the "creationTimestamp: null" field from the StatefulSet pod template metadata between Kubernetes versions 1.33 and 1.34. TITLE: The event handlers of job controller are slow
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

The event handlers in job controller are much slower than other controllers. It can cause the ring buffer in the processorListener to grow unbounded when the job churn is high enough.
The processing logic in the job controller events handler appears to be more complicated than other controllers. e.g. in [updateJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dbc2b0a5c7acc349ea71a14e49913661eaf708d2/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L464-L504), it invokes function `cleanupPodFinalizers` that lists the pods matching some selectors and the enqueue them to another queue. Similarly in [deleteJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dbc2b0a5c7acc349ea71a14e49913661eaf708d2/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L508-L524).

I added some instrumenting code to understand the latency of each event handler.
For job controller P99:
job add event handler: 0.080 ms
job update event handler: 3.075 ms
job delete event handler: 3.076 ms
pod add event handler: 0.136 ms
pod update event handler: 0.709 ms
pod delete event handler: 0.405 ms

For ttl-after-completion controller P99:
job add event handler: 0.0065 ms
job update event handler: 0.024 ms

T
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause of the slowness is that the job controller's event handlers perform complex and expensive operations directly within the event handler methods, such as listing pods and enqueuing them, instead of deferring such processing to the controller's main reconcile loop. This design leads to high latency and potential buildup of events, especially under high job churn.
FIX: Improve performance of the job controller when handling job update events.
FILES: pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go, pkg/controller/job/job_controller_test.go

TITLE: cronjob controller: reconsider log verbosity
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

We are running Kubernetes 1.25.5 and trying to configure kube-controller-manager to be less verbose when logging.
We run kube-controller-manager as a static pod created by Kubelet and use the following command where we pass `--v=0`:
```
spec:
  containers:
  - command:
    - kube-controller-manager
    - --feature-gates=EphemeralContainers=true,TopologyAwareHints=true
    - --allocate-node-cidrs=true
    - --authentication-kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf
    - --authorization-kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf
    - --cluster-cidr=10.6.0.0/16
    - --configure-cloud-routes=false
    - --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf
    - --leader-elect=true
    - --node-monitor-grace-period=120s
    - --root-ca-file=/etc/kubernetes/ssl/ca.pem
    - --service-account-private-key-file=/etc/kubernetes/ssl/signing-key.pem
    - --use-service-account-credentials
    - --v=0
    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.25.5
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    livenessProbe:
      failureThreshold: 3
      httpGet:
        host: 127.0.0.1
        path: /healthz
        po
ROOT CAUSE: The cronjob controller uses a global logging verbosity level of 3 for its event broadcaster, which is independent of the global -v flag passed to kube-controller-manager. As a result, event messages logged with verbosity 4 are always emitted if the global level is 3, ignoring the --v flag. This causes noisy logs even when low verbosity (e.g., --v=0) is requested. The root cause is the broadcaster's logging level is hardcoded and does not depend on the passed verbosity flag.
FIX: kube-controller-manager: increase the global level for broadcaster's logging to 3 so that users can ignore event messages by lowering the logging level. It reduces information noise.
FILES: cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/apps.go, cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/autoscaling.go, cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/core.go, cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/networking.go, pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go, pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go, pkg/controller/deployment/deployment_controller.go, pkg/controller/disruption/disruption.go, pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go, pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller_test.go

TITLE: CronJob gets stuck when jobs quota is reached
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

We (in Booking.com) run CronJobs in Kubernetes clusters with ResourceQuota's defined. When quota for # of jobs is reached we observed that CronJobs:
1. stop scheduling new jobs (because quota is reached),
2. don't clean the old jobs (despite # of jobs > history allows and the fact that it would unblock the CronJob new Jobs). 

The only way to progress is to remove enough Jobs to make room for a new Job in namespace quota. When we do that manually, the CronJob kicks in.

The workaround we found around the internet is to specify `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` for the job template. But it's not ideal as it's not a history-based limit, but a time-based limit, and often you want to have the last N jobs to be around for debugging.

### What did you expect to happen?

When jobs quota is reached and # of cronjob jobs exceeds specified the history limit, these jobs are deleted giving room for new jobs to run.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: job-quota
  namespace: default
spec:
  hard:
    count/jobs.batch: "1"
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metad
ROOT CAUSE: The bug happened because when the cronjob controller failed to create a new Job due to hitting the resource quota limit, it aborted the iteration early without performing cleanup of old finished Jobs. This prevented the controller from deleting obsolete Jobs to free quota, causing a deadlock where new Jobs could never be scheduled.
FIX: Fixed an issue where a CronJob could fail to clean up Jobs when the ResourceQuota for Jobs had been reached.
FILES: pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go, pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2_test.go

TITLE: Job controller reports the count of ready pods with unnecessary delay
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

When Job controller is deleting pods the counter in the status.ready field does not reflect this properly (there is a delay until the cache is refreshed). This affects the scenarios of terminating job, suspended job, and excess pods deleted.

### What did you expect to happen?

The ready field is updated as soon as the delete requests are sent successfully, in sync with the status.active field.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. To see this you can scale down a job, use the following yaml:
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: simple-job
spec:
  completions: 2
  parallelism: 2
  completionMode: Indexed
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: 'worker'
        image: python
        command:
        - python3
        - -c
        - |
          import time
          time.sleep(300)
```

2. Watch for the job updates with the following watcher:
```
kubectl get jobs -w --output-watch-events -ocustom-columns=EVENT:.type,NAME:.object.metadata.name,READY:.object.status.ready,ACTIVE:.object.status.active,TERMINATING:.object.status.terminat
ROOT CAUSE: The bug happened because the Job controller counts ready pods only among the currently active pods during deletion, but since the number of active pods updates asynchronously and may decrease after the count was made, the ready pod count does not get updated promptly to reflect pods that are terminating or deleted. This lag causes stale ready counts until the cache refreshes.
FIX: Now the .status.ready field is tracked faster when active Pods are deleted, specifically when Job is failed, gets suspended or has too many active pods
FILES: pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go, pkg/controller/job/job_controller_test.go

TITLE: Kubernetes Jobs API rapid-fire scheduling doesnt honor exponential backoff characteristics
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

# Problem

The job controller appears to "rapidly reschedule" several pods at the same time (without backing off) which ultimately appears almost like a batch or gang scheduling workflow.  

... This is the opposite of what the job docs say, bc they clearly state :
```
 The back-off limit is set by default to 6. Failed Pods associated with the Job are recreated by the Job controller with an exponential back-off delay (10s, 20s, 40s ...) capped at six minutes.
```
So, rather then, 

- 10, 20, 40, 80 wait times between trying things we are seeing
- 0, 3, 3, 3, 3 second wait times before pods are being retried

This is in the 1.25 release, but not sure if it also happens earlier.  You can see this in the latest kind version. 



### What did you expect to happen?

Jobs wouldnt schedule the same pod at rapid fire intervals

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

# Details 

Thanks to Ryan for this reproducer: 
```
apiVersion: batch/v1

kind: Job

metadata:

  name: backoff-exp

spec:

  backoffLimit: 100

  template:

    spec:

      containers:

        - name: die

          image: ubuntu


ROOT CAUSE: The Job controller's back-off logic was coupled with the workqueue's back-off mechanism, causing rapid rescheduling of failed pods without proper exponential delay. This coupling meant multiple pod failures within a reconciliation cycle did not properly aggregate back-off delays, resulting in retries being scheduled too frequently and ignoring exponential backoff requirements.
FIX: The job controller back-off logic is now decoupled from workqueue. In case of parallelism > 1, if there are multiple new failures in a reconciliation cycle, all the failures are taken into account to compute the back-off. Previously, the back-off kicked in for all types of failures; with this change, only pod failures are taken into account. If the back-off limits exceeds, the job is marked as failed immediately; before this change, the job is marked as failed in the next back-off.
FILES: pkg/controller/job/backoff_utils.go, pkg/controller/job/backoff_utils_test.go, pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go, pkg/controller/job/job_controller_test.go, test/integration/job/job_test.go

diagnosis.root_cause: When resuming a suspended Job, the Job controller unconditionally resets the Job's status.startTime to the current time. However, the strict validation logic forbids changing status.startTime for unsuspended Jobs if it was previously set. This causes a validation error because the updated startTime differs from the old value, but the controller always tries to update it on resume, triggering the validation failure.

claims.text: The job controller code in pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go unconditionally resets job.Status.StartTime to the current time when resuming a suspended Job, causing an update to the startTime even when it should remain unchanged.

The validation logic in pkg/apis/batch/validation/validation.go rejects changes to status.startTime if the Job is not suspended and the previous startTime was not nil, causing the validation error upon Job resume.

Together, the unconditional update of startTime on resume combined with the strict validation forbidding such updates causes the Job controller to fail validation and log errors when resuming a suspended Job.

TITLE: `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks apiserver readiness for 1 minute if discovery cannot be completed
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

I’m seeing some odd behavior with 1.28.2 that was not present in earlier releases, with regards to aggregated api services. It appears that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` is now blocking the apiserver from becoming ready for 1 minute, if discovery for an aggregated apiservice is not available when the apiserver is started. Note that this only happens if the apiservice is marked available when the apiserver is started; if it is unavailable at startup (Available status: false), or the service has no endpoints, the health check does not block and readyz returns `ok` without delay.

I am seeing this behavior in 1.28.1 and 1.28.2, but not v1.27.6 or v1.27.5

### What did you expect to happen?

apiserver becomes ready without any additional delays

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy metrics-server to a Kubernetes cluster
2. Wait for api registration for `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` to complete (Available status is `true`).
3. Kill the kubelet and pods on the node hosting the metrics-server pod, such that the metrics-server service continues to show available endpoints, but the endpoint is 
ROOT CAUSE: The bug was caused by the AddUpdateAPIService function simultaneously adding and updating the APIService spec during startup, rather than deferring the spec update to be handled asynchronously by the controller. This synchronous update caused race conditions and health check blocking when discovery failed, leading to readiness delays.
FIX: Fix regression with adding aggregated apiservices panicking and affected health check introduced in release v1.28.0

TITLE: kube-apiserver doesn't reload the kubelet client certificate/key on each logs query
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

We bootstrap our clusters with kubeadm (through clusterapi), but provide our own end certs to shorten the certificate validity period.

Because of the shortened validity period, we rotate the file-based endcerts frequently. Recently we started noticing that after performing a certificate rotation, usage of `kubectl logs` was failing with

```sh
error: You must be logged in to the server (the server has asked for the client to provide credentials)
```

From there, we looked at the kube-apiserver and kubelet logs and found log lines like the following:

```
"Unable to authenticate the request due to an error" err="verifying certificate SN=<REMOVED>, SKID=<REMOVED>, AKID=<REMOVED> failed: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2022-12-17T02:31:09Z is after 2022-12-17T00:16:30Z"
```

So it looks like kube-apiserver didn't reload the new kubelet client certificate. This issue typically goes away if we restart the kube-apiserver container or continue to run `kubectl logs` in a loop.

### What did you expect to happen?

Being able to replace/rotate the kube-apiserver kubelet client certificate/key without causing failure for any 
ROOT CAUSE: The kube-apiserver did not reload or re-establish the TLS connections to the kubelet when the client certificate files used for authentication were rotated. Instead, it reused existing cached TLS connections which retained the old, expired certificates, causing authentication failures on subsequent requests such as 'kubectl logs'.
FIX: The Kubernetes API server now correctly detects and closes existing TLS connections when its client certificate file for kubelet authentication has been rotated.

SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

Initially reported at 1.24.10, but it seems to be present in master as well:

We observe that a part of apiservices objects have been removed by "system:apiserver" right after the kubernetes upgrade.

It looks like there is race between "autoregister controller" [1] deleting apiservices and "crd-autoregister controller" populating a map of desired apiservices, i.e. in logs we see:
```
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070841Z Starting autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070858Z Waiting for caches to sync for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071116Z Starting crd-autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071128Z Waiting for caches to sync for crd-autoregister
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.270943Z Caches are synced for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.471323Z Caches are synced for crd-autoregister
```

The unwanted APIServices delete happened at 14:21:35.438 GMT so between crd-autoregister sync and autoregister controller.

It looks like we attempt to wait with "autoregister controller" for crd-autoregister to initialize here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c1d2d4295f9b4eb12bfbf6429fdf989f2ca8a02
ROOT CAUSE: The server startup code incorrectly detects whether the CustomResourceDefinitions (CRD) API is enabled by checking the wrong condition or using improper logic. As a result, the autoregister controller proceeds to reconcile and delete APIService objects before the CRD controller has synced, causing a race condition where APIs for existing CRDs are mistakenly deleted at startup.
FIX: Fixes a bug at kube-apiserver start where APIService objects for custom resources could be deleted and recreated.
FILES: cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go, cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go, cmd/kube-apiserver/app/testing/testserver.go, test/integration/examples/apiserver_test.go

TITLE: After upgrading to version v1.27.3 `Adding GroupVersion` is repeated in the api-server log
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

I upgraded k3s from `v1.26.2+k3s1` to `v1.27.3+k3s1` and noticed a log message `Adding GroupVersion` is repeated in the k3s.log. I also see this message when deploying a container that uses apiserver aggregation, such as `kubevirt` in other distros such as `minikube` in the api-server log.

### What did you expect to happen?

The message should not repeated in the logs.  This causes a nuisance and the logs eventually are rotated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Upgrade kubernetes to `v1.27.3` and install a container that uses uses apiserver aggregation such as `calico` or `kubevirt`.  

### Anything else we need to know?

For reference the original issue was reported here:
https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/issues/8038

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
WARNING: This version information is deprecated and will be replaced with the output from kubectl version --short.  Use --output=yaml|json to get the full version.
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"27", GitVersion:"v1.27.4", GitCommit:"fa3d7990104d7c1f16943a67f11b154b71f6a132", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2023-07-19T12:20:54Z
ROOT CAUSE: The logging of "Adding GroupVersion" occurs regardless of whether the discovery document has actually changed. This causes repeated log messages even when no updates occur to the aggregated API services, leading to log spam. The root cause is missing conditional logic to check if the discovery information has changed before logging the addition of a GroupVersion.
FIX: Fixes bug where Adding GroupVersion log line is constantly repeated without any group version changes
FILES: staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/discovery/aggregated/handler.go

diagnosis.root_cause: The bug occurs because the alpha API version check compares the full semantic version including patch level (e.g., 1.34.1 vs 1.34), incorrectly triggering warnings when the patch version differs though the major/minor versions match. Thus, the code logs spurious warnings about version mismatch at startup when the alpha API emulation version does not exactly equal the binary version, failing to ignore patch version differences.

claims.text: The code snippet compares the binary version and emulated alpha API version using .EqualTo(), which includes patch version in equality check, causing warnings when patch versions differ but major.minor are the same.

The log warnings about alpha API versions mentioning emulated version 1.34 instead of binary's 1.34.1 confirm the check is based on exact equality including patch version, leading to spurious logs on startup.

Discussion in the ticket confirms that the comparison should only consider major and minor versions, not patch, showing this defect is from overly strict version equality check causing start-up log spam.

TITLE: DRA: Kubelet doesn't report anything when it fails to prepare dynamic resources
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

When `PrepareResource` API fails there is no way to understand what happens because error is not reported.

### What did you expect to happen?

Error should be either logged or, better event should be recorded, so user would see it in the `kubelet describe pod` output.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Apply this patch to the kubernetes sources:
```
diff --git a/test/e2e/dra/test-driver/deploy/example/pod-inline.yaml b/test/e2e/dra/test-driver/deploy/example/pod-inline.yaml
index 13b177c8426..c494a54b287 100644
--- a/test/e2e/dra/test-driver/deploy/example/pod-inline.yaml
+++ b/test/e2e/dra/test-driver/deploy/example/pod-inline.yaml
@@ -28,6 +28,7 @@ kind: Pod
 metadata:
   name: test-inline-claim
 spec:
+  nodeName: 127.0.0.1
   restartPolicy: Never
   containers:
   - name: with-resource
```

2. Create a pod: ```kubectl apply -f test/e2e/dra/test-driver/deploy/example/pod-inline.yaml```
3. Get the pod details: 
```
kubectl.sh describe pod test-inline-claim 
Using image: cos-97-16919-294-27 from project: cos-cloud as master image
Using image: cos-97-16919-294-27 from project: cos-cloud as node image
ROOT CAUSE: The Kubelet's dynamic resource preparation logic did not report or log errors when the PrepareResource API failed, resulting in a lack of visibility into why pods were pending due to resource preparation failures. This absence of error reporting made it impossible for users to understand the root cause of pod scheduling issues related to dynamic resources.
FIX: Dynamic Resource Allocation: log a error and submit an event when Kubelet fails to prepare dynamic resources

TITLE: structured-merge-diff supports only  'set' type for associative list
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

kube-apiserver has has this kind of entries in log
```
E0126 00:39:45.253562       1 fieldmanager.go:210] "[SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields" err="failed to convert new object (default/test-inline-claim; /v1, Kind=Pod) to smd typed: .spec.containers[name=\"with-resource\"].resources.claims: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" VersionKind="/, Kind=" namespace="default" name="test-inline-claim"
E0126 00:39:46.700727       1 fieldmanager.go:210] "[SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields" err="failed to convert new object (default/test-inline-claim-resource; resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1, Kind=ResourceClaim) to smd typed: .status.reservedFor: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" VersionKind="/, Kind=" namespace="default" name="test-inline-claim-resource"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected those lines not to appear in kube-apiserver logs, and structured-merge-diff to support map types, like the comment says at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/sigs.k8s.io/structured-merge-diff/v4/typed/helpers.go#L233

### How can we reprod
ROOT CAUSE: The bug happened because the structured-merge-diff library used by the apiserver expects associative lists with keys to be of 'set' type, but the code contained an associative list without keys that had map-type elements. This usage violates the library's expectations and causes conversion failures when updating managed fields.
FIX: A fix in the resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1/ResourceClaim API avoids harmless (?) ".status.reservedFor: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" errors in the apiserver. Validation now rejects the incorrect reuse of the same UID in different entries.

We have k8s cluster with  Scalable function DRA driver deployed. 
We created Pod with resource claim to allocate Scalable function to Pod. 
When reboot the worker node the Pod with with Scalable function  failed to start with error [1].
The reason for the error is that PrepareResource is not called after reboot so we didn't create Scalable function  resource and prepare CDI file for it. 



[1] - Aug 09 09:58:45 cloud-dev-44 kubelet[1851]: E0809 09:58:45.873380    1851 remote_runtime.go:302] "CreateContainer in sandbox from runtime service failed" err="rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create containerd container: CDI device injection failed: unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/net-sf=mlx5_core.sf.3" podSandboxID="5ce2a000bf64e9b7d9570a95e53718f9369376b866b22fbbeed22f8faca2c88b"

TITLE: DRA: kubelet: crash when plugin returns nil UnprepareResourceResponse
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

protobuf doesn't require that objects get encoded when they are empty. This can lead to a nil pointer in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/124042 (although that's probably an error because some information is needed) and in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/20d0ab7ae808aaddb1556c3c38ca0607663c50ac/staging/src/k8s.io/kubelet/pkg/apis/dra/v1alpha3/api.pb.go#L255 (happened in practice).

The result is a crash of kubelet:
```
E0305 14:50:50.162844   10432 runtime.go:79] Observed a panic: "invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference" (runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference)
goroutine 883 [running]:
k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.logPanic({0x3de2d20?, 0x6fc0d90})
	/go/src/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:75 +0x85
k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.HandleCrash({0x0, 0x0, 0x0?})
	/go/src/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:49 +0x6b
panic({0x3de2d20?, 0x6fc0d90?})
	/usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:914 +0x21f
k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra.(*ManagerImpl).UnprepareResources(0xc00097b998, 0xc000d48900)
	/go/src/kubernetes/pkg/
ROOT CAUSE: The kubelet code did not handle the case where the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver returns a nil pointer for the NodePrepareResources or NodeUnprepareResources response. Because protobuf encoding can omit empty objects leading to nil pointers, this caused a nil pointer dereference panic in the kubelet.
FIX: kubelet no longer crashes when a DRA driver returns a nil as part of the Node(Un)PrepareResources response instead of an empty struct (did not affect drivers written in Go, first showed up with a driver written in Rust).

TITLE: Scheduling Pods with dynamic resources and using the Pod `.spec.nodeName` field fails
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

The combination of using the Pod spec nodeName field with the `DynamicResources` scheduler plugin (currently feature-gated) doesn't work. No surprise really as the nodeName field effective bypasses the `DynamicResources` scheduler plugin running, and something rather clever would need to be invented to make things to work. But this is still a bit of a regression compared to the old device plugin model which doesn't have a similar limitation.  @pohly as the author of the dynamic resources feature can explain what could maybe be created to fix this.

Granted, forcing scheduling even with a device plugin resource may or may not succeed at the node level depending on the availability of said plugin resources at the node, but with dynamic resources the failure seems to be currently guaranteed.

The use-case for this is such that the Kubernetes scheduler is effectively being preceded by some other scheduler which runs earlier (say, some HPC framework) which is giving the Pods the node names and somehow knows that there will be enough resources, and then the workloads ought to land in the specified node and the container related work is then handled normally from t
ROOT CAUSE: The root cause is that when a Pod has its spec.nodeName field set (indicating it is pre-assigned to a specific node), the Dynamic Resources scheduler plugin is bypassed and does not run. Since this plugin is responsible for managing resource claims and reservations, bypassing it leads to the pod being rejected or failing to run because its resource claims are not properly allocated or reserved. This limitation arises because the scheduler plugin is skipped when the pod is pre-scheduled, preventing the dynamic resource allocation logic from executing.
FIX: kube-controller-manager: the dynamic resource controller steps in when a pod got created such that the scheduler ignores it (i.e. spec.nodeName is set) and then takes care of triggering delayed resource claim allocation and/or reserving a claim for the pod.
FILES: cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/core.go, pkg/controller/resourceclaim/controller.go, pkg/controller/resourceclaim/controller_test.go, plugin/pkg/auth/authorizer/rbac/bootstrappolicy/controller_policy.go, staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/controller/controller.go, test/e2e/dra/dra.go, test/e2e/dra/test-driver/app/controller.go, test/integration/util/util.go

diagnosis.root_cause: The bug occurs because the kubelet matches resource claim names exactly between the pod's container resource claims and the resource claim objects received from the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) plugin. However, for resource claims generated from templates, the names seen in the pod spec differ from the actual resource claim object names, causing the matching logic to fail. This mismatch leads to kubelet not associating health statuses with these resource claims and skipping the reporting of health information.

claims.text: The code in pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go compares container.Resources.Claims claim.Name with claimInfo.ClaimName using exact equality. This fails for claims generated via templates because their names differ, resulting in the "Could not find matching resource claim in container spec" log entries and missing health reporting.

TITLE: Updating the nodeAffinity of gated pods having nil affinity is not allowed
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

When a gated pod is created with nil affinity and a user/controller tries to update its nodeAffinity, the validation fails.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod gets updated with the new affinity as per rules in [KEP-3838](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/commit/ac65b5853a9a5b8fb77a8c3069c07780057a4c9e)

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod as in the following using `kubectl create`:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  generateName: example-no-affinity-
spec:
  schedulingGate:
    - name: "example-gate" # just to ignore any other component that should add a scheduling gate
  containers:
    - name: example-container
      image: 'quay.io/openshifttest/hello-openshift:1.2.0'
```
2. Try to update the pod as with:
```shell
 kubectl patch pod example-no-affinity-hz4lz -p '{"spec":{"affinity":{"nodeAffinity":{"requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution":{"nodeSelectorTerms":[{"matchExpressions":[{"key":"expr","operator":"In","values":["value"]}]}]}}}}}'

```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```cons
ROOT CAUSE: The validation logic incorrectly prohibits updates to the nodeAffinity field of pods that initially have a nil affinity. The update logic expects changes only to a limited set of fields, and since nil affinity and empty affinity structs differ, the update is wrongly rejected as invalid. This causes the update to fail when the pod's affinity was originally nil and is updated to a non-nil value.
FIX: Updating the nodeAffinity of gated pods having nil affinity should be allowed
FILES: pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go, pkg/apis/core/validation/validation_test.go, test/integration/pods/pods_test.go

TITLE: kubelet (1.27.1) fails to mount a hostPath volume for a static pod
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

This is a bit hard to reproduce, as it happens in a very specific setup, the problems only happens with `kubelet` 1.27.1, downgrading to 1.26.4 fixes the problem.

In a single-node cluster controlplane pods run as static pods, Rook/Ceph is deployed, and some PVs/PVCs backed by Ceph.

After a unclean shutdown related to some PVs backed by Ceph not being unmounted (this is not a Kubernetes), the `kubelet` which comes up after a reboot doesn't start controlplane static pods, which essentially blocks every other pod from starting (as API server is done).

After a reboot, kubelet is running, but it keeps reporting an error about static pods like:

```
172.20.0.2: {"ts":1683110056228.5916,"caller":"kubelet/kubelet.go:1875","msg":"Unable to attach or mount volumes for pod; skipping pod","pod":{"name":"kube-apiserver-talos-default-controlplane-1","namespace":"kube-system"},"err":"unmounted volumes=[audit secrets config], unattached volumes=[], failed to process volumes=[]: timed out waiting for the condition"}
```

All of the volumes are `hostPath` volumes in a static pod:

```yaml
        volumes:
            - hostPath:
                path: /system/s
ROOT CAUSE: The bug was caused by the kubelet's volume reconstruction logic incorrectly relying on the availability of the CSIDriver API objects to determine if a volume is attachable during startup. When the kubelet started, it sometimes lacked connection to the API server and thus could not query the CSIDriver, causing the CSI volume reconstruction to hang and prevent static pods with volumes from starting. The code assumed API server availability that might not exist during early kubelet startup, leading to indefinite waits for volume conditions.
FIX: Fixed kubelet startup getting stuck with `NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` feature enabled and a CSI volume present in /var/lib/kubelet/pods.
FILES: pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/cache/actual_state_of_world.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/cache/actual_state_of_world_test.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_new.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_new_test.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct_common.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct_new.go, pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct_new_test.go

TITLE: [Bug] Missing constraint and validation for label selector's values
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

Hello,
There are some [constraints](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/#syntax-and-character-set) that label selector's `values` need to conform:
>* must be 63 characters or less (can be empty),
>* unless empty, must begin and end with an alphanumeric character ([a-z0-9A-Z]),
>* could contain dashes (-), underscores (_), dots (.), and alphanumerics between.

Every label selctor's `values` will be checked [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e5ba5cd2b0d3bddd4a0393b98fde14960f31a33c/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/validation/validation.go#L166C1-L175C2), and when values is not conforming these constraints, an error will be returned.

`nodeAfffinty.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms.matchExpressions.values` also needs to conform these constraints (because `matchExpressions` will be parsed as a label selector), but cccording to the [concept documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#operators) and the [API documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.31/#nodeselectorrequirement-v1-core), 
ROOT CAUSE: The underlying cause is that the system did not validate the values in NodeSelectorRequirement against label value constraints during pod creation. This lack of validation allowed invalid strings to be accepted, leading to parse errors during scheduling and causing the scheduler to reject the node selector terms silently without warning the user.
FIX: kubenetes starts validating NodeSelectorRequirement's values when creating pods.
FILES: pkg/api/node/util.go, pkg/api/persistentvolume/util.go, pkg/api/pod/util.go, pkg/api/pod/util_test.go, pkg/api/pod/warnings.go, pkg/api/pod/warnings_test.go, pkg/apis/core/helper/helpers.go, pkg/apis/core/helper/helpers_test.go, pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go, pkg/apis/core/validation/validation_test.go

TITLE: kube-proxy in LocalModeNodeCIDR mode may cache stale Node.PodCIDR if the Node object is recreated
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

If `LocalModeNodeCIDR` is true, kube-proxy reads the `Node.PodCIDR` value and uses it to determine whether or not traffic is local to the Node.

In certain cases (e.g. when kube-proxy runs before the Node information has been completely updated), it is possible for kube-proxy to read and store a stale `PodCIDR` value. This will cause kube-proxy to route traffic incorrectly as the local traffic determination is no longer correct.

Note: PodCIDR is immutable once set but it is possible to delete and recreate the Node object to get into this state. (yes, this can happen)



### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy should detect this state and reconfigure/restart with the newly updated `PodCIDR`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Recreate the Node object with a different PodCIDR after kube-proxy has started on the Node.

### Kubernetes version

Impacts all current versions that support `LocalModeNodeCIDR`

### Cloud provider

<details>
Observed for GCE preemptible/spot VMs, but is a generic problem.
</details>
ROOT CAUSE: kube-proxy reads the Node object's PodCIDR at startup and caches it, but does not update this cached PodCIDR when the Node object is deleted and recreated with a different PodCIDR. Therefore, kube-proxy continues to use the stale PodCIDR for local traffic determination, causing incorrect routing.
FIX: kube-proxy, will restart in case it detects that the Node assigned pod.Spec.PodCIDRs have changed
FILES: cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go, cmd/kube-proxy/app/server_others.go, cmd/kube-proxy/app/server_others_test.go, pkg/proxy/node.go, pkg/proxy/node_test.go, pkg/proxy/topology.go, pkg/proxy/topology_test.go

diagnosis.root_cause: The bug happens because kubelet relies on a node object from its local informer cache to perform node affinity checks. When the cache is stale and does not reflect recent label updates on the node (which the scheduler sees correctly), kubelet wrongly rejects pods with 'NodeAffinity failed'. The defect mechanism is a stale informer cache used by kubelet without a fallback to fresh data, causing kubelet to operate on outdated node labels during admission checks.

claims.text: Kubelet performs node affinity admission checks using a cached node object obtained from the nodeLister, an informer cache, so if this cache is stale, kubelet observes outdated node labels.
The nodeLister cache can be stale after node label updates, causing kubelet to reject pods even though the scheduler successfully schedules them due to fresh label knowledge.

The diagnosis and proposed fixes in the ticket explicitly describe that the issue is stale informer cache causing kubelet node affinity failures and propose fallback strategies to mitigate stale data.

TITLE: server-side dry-run apply on custom resource fails no-op conversion with error about missing metadata
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

On a new 1.27 kubernetes cluster, Using server-side dry-run to apply a custom resource with an older version results in the following error:

```
$  kubectl apply --server-side --dry-run=server -fclusters/my-clusters/image-repo.yaml --field-manager=kustomize-controller

Error from server: failed to prune fields: failed add back owned items: failed to convert pruned object at version image.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1beta2: conversion for image.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1beta2, Kind=ImagePolicy returned invalid metadata in object at index 1: missing metadata in converted object

TITLE: Status manager does not normalize ephemeral container statuses
SYMPTOM: ### What happened?

`EphemeralContainerStatuses` is not normalized in 	`normalizeStatus()` in the status manager:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cade1dddd81eba338df85de7b5d17324a87243b5/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L1026-L1043

This does not seem to cause any user facing problem because `EphemeralContainerStatuses` is sorted before passed to the status manager and timestamps are normalized at marshaling to create a patch:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cade1dddd81eba338df85de7b5d17324a87243b5/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2336

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cade1dddd81eba338df85de7b5d17324a87243b5/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L873
